title: Beyond Entropy: Correctness-Aware Advantage Shaping via Contrastive Policy Optimization
hook: RLVR shapes rewards with entropy, but entropy can't tell useful uncertainty from confusion. CPO swaps in token-level disagreement — and shows on-policy distillation was a special case of it.
key_points: Problem: entropy-based advantage shaping in RLVR can't separate useful uncertainty from detrimental confusion, weakening it as a correctness signal.
CPO's fix: token-level contrastive disagreement between a reference-guided and a vanilla generation distribution — shown both theoretically and empirically to track token-level correctness.
Unifying claim: on-policy distillation falls out as a special case of CPO, when an external teacher model instantiates the reference distribution.
CPO also resolves RLVR's zero-advantage problem, where groups of uniformly right or uniformly wrong rollouts otherwise contribute no learning signal.
Correct and incorrect responses drive exploitation and exploration respectively; balancing both gives CPO's best results, beating entropy-based RLVR on in- and out-of-domain benchmarks.
content_html: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) typically uses entropy to decide which tokens get more or less credit during training — but entropy conflates useful uncertainty with pure confusion, making it a weak correctness signal. Contrastive Policy Optimization (CPO) replaces it with a sharper one: the token-level disagreement between a reference-guided generation distribution and the model's own vanilla one, which the authors show — both theoretically and empirically — reliably tracks whether a token is correct.
extra_html: CPO also reframes a familiar technique: on-policy distillation turns out to be a special case of CPO, recovered when the reference distribution is instantiated by an external teacher model. The same signal resolves RLVR's zero-advantage problem, where a group of rollouts that's uniformly right or uniformly wrong normally teaches the model nothing. Across in-domain and out-of-domain benchmarks, CPO substantially outperforms entropy-based RLVR baselines; further analysis shows correct and incorrect responses naturally drive exploitation and exploration respectively, and balancing the two is what makes CPO work best.

related.title: GRPO, Dr. GRPO, and DAPO Are Three Operations on One Number: The Group-Standard-Deviation Identity
related.hook: GRPO, Dr. GRPO, and DAPO look like three separate fixes to reasoning RL — this paper proves they're just three settings of one dial: how much weight to put on a group's disagreement.

related.title: GRPO: Group Relative Policy Optimization
related.hook: GRPO dropped the value network from PPO and scored each answer against a group of sampled siblings — the cheap RL recipe that made DeepSeek-R1's reasoning trainable.

related.title: On the Geometry of On-Policy Distillation
related.hook: On-policy distillation isn't a midpoint between fine-tuning and RL — it carves its own narrow path through parameter space, locking into a low-dimensional subspace early in training.

flashcards.prompt: What signal does CPO use instead of entropy for advantage shaping in RLVR?
flashcards.back_html: Token-level contrastive disagreement between a reference-guided generation distribution and the model's own vanilla distribution — shown to reliably track token-level correctness where entropy can't.

flashcards.prompt: How does CPO relate to on-policy distillation?

choices.text: On-policy distillation is a special case of CPO, when the reference distribution comes from an external teacher model
On-policy distillation is an alternative used only when no reference model is available
CPO is a preprocessing step that must run before on-policy distillation can start

flashcards.explanation_html: CPO's contrastive-disagreement framework is general; plugging in an external teacher as the reference distribution recovers on-policy distillation as one instance of it.

flashcards.prompt: What is RLVR's 'zero-advantage problem', which CPO resolves?
flashcards.back_html: When a group of sampled rollouts is uniformly right or uniformly wrong, standard advantage estimates collapse to zero and the group contributes no learning signal.

flashcards.prompt: According to the paper, what roles do correct and incorrect responses play during CPO training?

choices.text: Correct responses support exploitation and incorrect responses support exploration; balancing both gives the best performance
Correct responses are discarded and only incorrect responses drive learning
Both play identical roles and can be weighted equally with no tradeoff

flashcards.explanation_html: Correct and incorrect rollouts naturally specialize — correct ones reinforce exploitation, incorrect ones fuel exploration — and CPO's gains come from balancing the two.
